entries.name: ExtensionErrorCode
entries.doc: Why a call came back without its answer. `permission-denied`: the manifest does not ask for the permission. `no-project`: no project with a folder is open. `no-canvas`: no canvas is in front. `not-found`: what it names is not there. `outside-project`: a path leaves the project folder. `refused`: the machine or the person said no. `limit`: too many calls in a while. `timeout`: no answer in time. `unavailable`: the machine, or `server/`, cannot answer now. `failed`: anything else, with its message.
entries.code:
export type ExtensionErrorCode =
    | 'permission-denied'
    | 'no-project'
    | 'no-canvas'
    | 'not-found'
    | 'outside-project'
    | 'refused'
    | 'limit'
    | 'timeout'
    | 'unavailable'
    | 'failed';

entries.name: Result
entries.doc: What a call that can fail answers: its value, or why not. Only a wrong argument throws. A call with nothing to answer, a `Result<void>`, answers `{ ok: true, value: undefined }` with the key `value` there.
entries.code: export type Result<Value, Code extends string = ExtensionErrorCode> = { ok: true; value: Value } | { ok: false; error: { code: Code; message: string } };

entries.name: Json
entries.doc: A value as it crosses to the machine and back.
entries.code: export type Json = string | number | boolean | null | Json[] | { [key: string]: Json | undefined };

entries.name: Returned
entries.doc: What a method of `server/` answers once it crossed as JSON: `undefined`, and so a method that returns nothing, arrives as `null`.
entries.code: export type Returned<Value> = Value extends undefined | void ? null : Value;

entries.name: LazyComponent
entries.doc: A component is always handed over as a lazy import: `() => import('./Panel')`.
entries.code: export type LazyComponent<Props = {}> = () => Promise<{ default: ComponentType<Props> }>;

entries.name: Surface
entries.code: export type Surface<Props = {}> = { component: LazyComponent<Props> } | { frame: string };

entries.name: PanelHandle
NodeRef
ViewRef
ProjectRef
definePanel
entries.doc: `icon` names a Lucide icon. Without one, a surface shows the extension's `assets/icon.svg`.

entries.name: defineSidebarCard
entries.code: export function defineSidebarCard(card: { id: string; title: string; component: LazyComponent }): void;

entries.name: defineView
entries.doc: `params` is kept with the view in the project, so it is JSON. A view opened without them, as `New <title>` opens it, gets undefined.

entries.name: defineNode
defineCanvasOverlay
entries.doc: Over the whole canvas, under Ruimte's own controls such as the minimap in the bottom right. It lets clicks through; set `pointer-events: auto` on what takes them. With `space: 'canvas'` it draws in the canvas's own coordinates instead, over every node, panned and zoomed with them, so a node's `bounds` are where it stands. Neither draws while a node is maximized. On screen, Ruimte marks what stands at the bottom of the canvas with `data-canvas-floor`: `ledge` where something may stand on top, such as the dock, and `wall` where it may only walk up to, such as the minimap and a prompt card. Find them from your own element with `closest('[data-canvas-overlay]')`; one that fades away says so in its opacity.
entries.code: export function defineCanvasOverlay(overlay: { id: string; component: LazyComponent; space?: 'screen' | 'canvas' }): void;

entries.name: defineFileViewer
entries.doc: Opens every file with these extensions in your component, with Ruimte's own view one click away.

entries.name: defineMarkdownBlock
entries.doc: Draws a fenced block of this language in a chat and in markdown, on this client. Elsewhere it stays code.
entries.code: export function defineMarkdownBlock(block: { language: string; component: LazyComponent<{ source: string }> }): void;

entries.name: defineOverlay
entries.doc: Your own UI over the app: Ruimte draws the header with `title` and a close button, and animates it; you draw the body. `open` answers what `close` was given, or null when a person dismissed it.

entries.name: ToolCall
entries.doc: A call of a tool in a chat, as the thread holds it.

entries.name: defineToolResult
entries.doc: Draws these tools' calls in a chat, by their exact name, instead of the thread's own view.
entries.code: export function defineToolResult(result: { id: string; tools: string[]; component: LazyComponent<{ call: ToolCall }> }): void;

entries.name: definePaletteSource
entries.doc: Rows in the command palette for what a person types. It waits for a pause in the typing; a slow or failing one costs only its own rows.

entries.name: defineSlashCommand
entries.doc: After `/` in a chat. It expands into the prompt, and the person still sends it.
entries.code: export function defineSlashCommand(command: { name: string; description: string; run(args: string): string | Promise<string> }): void;

entries.name: defineReference
entries.doc: Things from outside the project for `#` in a chat. Picking one puts what `read` answers in the prompt.

entries.name: defineDiffViewer
entries.doc: Opens a changed file with these extensions in your component, with Ruimte's own diff one click away.
entries.code: export function defineDiffViewer(viewer: { id: string; title: string; extensions: string[]; component: LazyComponent<{ file: FileInfo; diff: string }> }): void;

entries.name: defineLanguage
entries.doc: A language of your own: the files it covers and the TextMate grammar the editor and the viewer color them with, so a language pack is more than a language server. `id` is what a language server of yours names under `languages`, in lowercase letters, digits and dashes. `extensions` are without the dot and `filenames` are whole names, such as `Lintelfile`. `grammar` is the path of a JSON file in your pack, at most 512 KB, read when the first such file opens. A language Ruimte knows itself keeps its own grammar. Proposed: name `languages` under `proposed` in the manifest.
entries.code: export function defineLanguage(language: { id: string; name: string; extensions: string[]; filenames?: string[]; grammar: string }): void;

entries.name: EditorDecoration
entries.doc: A mark in the margin of the editor, on one line or on every line up to `endLine`. Lines count from 1.

entries.name: defineEditorDecoration
entries.doc: Marks in the margin of the editor, such as coverage or what a linter found. Ruimte asks `provide` for a file when it opens in an editor, and again for every open file after `refresh()`. It reads only: you are told which file, never its text or the selection, and change nothing in it. At most 2000 marks per file; a mark with a line below 1 or a kind Ruimte does not know is left out. Proposed: name `editorDecorations` under `proposed` in the manifest.

entries.name: defineFileIcon
entries.doc: An icon from your pack, by its path, for files with these extensions.
entries.code: export function defineFileIcon(icon: { extensions: string[]; path: string }): void;

entries.name: defineVoiceAction
entries.doc: What a person can ask for by voice, through extension.voiceList and extension.voiceRun. It answers in words. Type `Input` after `parameters`, a JSON Schema.

entries.name: defineTemplate
entries.doc: New from a template, under Extensions in the canvas menu.

entries.name: defineCommand
entries.code: export function defineCommand(command: { id: string; title: string; run: () => void | Promise<void> }): void;

entries.name: SettingField
SettingGroup
entries.doc: A section of an extension's settings page: a title over a card of fields, like Ruimte's own settings.

entries.name: SettingsSection
entries.doc: Settings of your own component as a section of the settings navigation, beside Ruimte's own, instead of a page under Settings, Extensions. Ruimte gives a section only to the extensions it ships itself; any other extension's page stays under Extensions, and `ruimte extension dev` says so once. `label`, `description` and each row's words are keys of your `locales/`. A row of `search` leads to the `SettingsRow` of your page with that `searchId`.

entries.name: defineExtensionSettings
entries.doc: Your own component, or `fields` (one card) or `groups` (a card per group) that Ruimte draws. One call takes one of the three: with `fields` or `groups` beside it, `component` is left out. Read a field with `useSetting`; keys are unique across groups.

entries.name: useSetting
entries.code: export function useSetting<Value extends boolean | string>(key: string): Value;

entries.name: ProjectSettings
entries.doc: A section of a project's settings: `fields` (one card) or `groups` (a card per group) that Ruimte draws.

entries.name: defineProjectSettings
entries.doc: A section in the settings of a project, for a choice that belongs to one project, such as the service its shells open in. What a person chooses is kept on the machine per project, never in the project file, so every computer that opens the project reads the same. Read a field with `useProjectSetting`, and from `server/` with `projectSettings.get`. Proposed: name `projectSettings` under `proposed` in the manifest.
entries.code: export function defineProjectSettings(settings: ProjectSettings): void;

entries.name: useProjectSetting
entries.doc: A field of `defineProjectSettings` for the project in front, or its default while a person never chose.
entries.code: export function useProjectSetting<Value extends boolean | string>(key: string): Value;

entries.name: useTheme
entries.code: export function useTheme(): { side: 'light' | 'dark' };

entries.code: export function useChat(id: string): ChatSummary | null;

entries.name: Chat
entries.doc: Needs `agents.start`, since it opens the chat again when it is not running. A chat of the project in front as Ruimte draws it, its thread and its composer, by the id `agents.start` answered without a `folder`.
entries.code: export function Chat(props: { id: string }): ReactElement;

entries.name: AgentStatus
entries.doc: Where an agent is, the same word everywhere it shows.
entries.code: export type AgentStatus = 'idle' | 'running' | 'needsYou' | 'stopped';

entries.name: AgentActivity
entries.doc: What an agent works on, as its node shows it: a turn of its own, agents it handed work to, or only commands it left running. Null while it works on nothing, and while it waits on a person.
entries.code: export type AgentActivity = 'turn' | 'delegating' | 'background' | null;

SubagentInfo
entries.doc: A sub-agent at work for a chat. `node` is the node of a task the chat gave, `paused` while that task waits for a limit to lift.

entries.name: ChatSummary
entries.doc: A chat on the machine, as `chats.list` answers it. Its id is the id of its node.

entries.name: NodeInfo
FileInfo
BaseContext
entries.doc: What every slot, action and widget is told.

entries.name: SlotAnswer
entries.doc: `false` hides it, `true` shows it, an object also changes what it shows there.
entries.code: export type SlotAnswer = boolean | { title?: string; icon?: string; disabled?: boolean | string; badge?: string; order?: number };

entries.name: Slot
entries.code: export type Slot<Context> = true | ((context: BaseContext & Context) => SlotAnswer);

entries.name: SlotContexts
entries.doc: What each place tells.

entries.name: SlotName
entries.code: export type SlotName = keyof SlotContexts;

entries.name: Slots

entries.name: ContextOf
entries.code: export type ContextOf<Place extends SlotName> = { [Key in Place]: BaseContext & SlotContexts[Key] }[Place];

entries.name: ActionHandle
entries.doc: Runs the action from code, with what its `run` reads beside the context of the window in front.

entries.name: defineAction
entries.doc: While `run` is pending, its nodes show a spinner that also stops it through `signal`, and a throw reaches the person. Without `slots` it only shows where a menu puts it, and gets that menu's context. Type it with `defineAction<Context>`.

entries.name: MenuItem
entries.code: export type MenuItem = ActionHandle | 'separator' | { title: string; run(): void; checked?: boolean } | { title: string; items: MenuItem[] };

entries.doc: A menu of your own: a submenu in a menu, a dropdown in a bar.

entries.name: defineWidget
entries.doc: Your own React in a slot.

entries.name: ServerClient
entries.doc: Each method calls `server/` on the machine in front and answers a Result: `failed` with the message of what it threw, `not-found` for a method it lacks, `unavailable` while it cannot run. `.use()` suspends until it answers, and keeps that answer for the same arguments until `.reload()` with them drops it, or the connection to the machine comes back. Every surface that read it then asks again. The value crosses as JSON, see {@link Returned}.

entries.name: useServer
entries.code: export function useServer<Server>(): ServerClient<Server>;

entries.name: ServerCalls
entries.doc: Each method of `server/` as {@link ServerClient} calls it, without `.use()` and `.reload()`, which only a component has.

entries.name: getServer
entries.doc: `server/` outside a component, such as in the `run` of a command or an action. Each call goes to the machine in front when it is made.
entries.code: export function getServer<Server>(): ServerCalls<Server>;

entries.name: useServerEvent
entries.doc: Hears what `emit` says in `server/`, with the payload it was given.

entries.name: useNodeData
entries.code: export function useNodeData<Data>(): [Data, (next: Data) => void];

entries.doc: `computer` stays on this computer. `project` and `machine` live on the machine, where `server/` reads `machine` keys too.
entries.code: export function useStorage<Value>(key: string, initial: Value, scope?: 'computer' | 'project' | 'machine'): [Value, (next: Value) => void];

entries.name: storage
entries.doc: The `computer` storage of `useStorage` outside a component, which every window of this computer shares. `set` answers `limit` when the computer refused to keep it; `watch` calls back when any window, this one too, changed the key.

entries.name: Result
entries.doc: What a call that can fail answers: its value, or why not. Only a wrong argument throws. A call with nothing to answer, a `Result<void>`, answers `{ ok: true, value: undefined }` with the key `value` there.

ProjectRef
AgentStatus

entries.code: export type AgentStatus = 'idle' | 'running' | 'needsYou' | 'stopped';

entries.name: ChatSummary
entries.doc: A chat on the machine, as `chats.list` answers it. Its id is the id of its node.

entries.name: defineServer
entries.doc: What the client can call. The default export of `server/index.ts`. A method that throws reaches the client as `failed`, with its message.
entries.code: export function defineServer<Api extends Record<string, (...args: never[]) => Promise<unknown>>>(api: Api): Api;

entries.name: ServerEvents
entries.doc: The machine's events `server/` can follow, with what each says.

entries.name: onEvent
entries.doc: Follows a machine event, behind its permission; any other name is refused. With `filter.project` only the events of that project are heard. Set `"autostart": true` to follow them with no client open.

entries.name: emit
entries.doc: Says something to every client of this machine, where `useServerEvent(name)` hears `payload`, or undefined without one.
entries.code: export function emit<Payload>(name: string, payload?: Payload): void;

entries.name: defineNodeContext
entries.doc: What an agent reads of a node along a line, also with no client open.
entries.code: export function defineNodeContext<Data>(nodeType: string, read: (node: { data: Data }) => Promise<{ text: string }[]> | { text: string }[]): void;

entries.name: defineAgentTool
entries.doc: Needs `agents.tools`. Any agent Ruimte starts on this machine can then find it with `tool_list` and call it with `tool_run`. Having it starts `server/` with the machine, since an agent can only find what is running. It answers in text. Type `Input` after `parameters`, a JSON Schema.

entries.name: schedule
entries.doc: Needs the permission `clock`. Runs on this process's own clock: `every` is like 30s, 5m or 1h, of at least 10 seconds and at most 596 hours.
entries.code: export function schedule(task: { id: string; every: string; run(): void | Promise<void> }): void;

entries.name: agents
chats
entries.doc: `list` and `read` need `chats.read`, `send` needs `chats.send`.

entries.name: ProjectInfo
entries.doc: A project of this machine, as a provider is asked about it.

entries.name: SpawnDescription
entries.doc: What a provider has Ruimte start: a program and its arguments. Ruimte runs it, so the session, its scrollback, its status and its stop stay Ruimte's, and the provider never reads what the program writes.

entries.name: defineTerminalProfile
entries.doc: Needs `terminals.profiles`. Proposed: name `terminalProfiles` under `proposed` in the manifest, and the id under `provides.terminalProfiles`, which is how the menu of a new terminal lists it before `server/` runs. Picking it starts `server/` and asks `spawn`; `available` hides it in a project where it has nothing to open, asked while `server/` runs. Throws for an id the manifest does not list.

entries.name: LaunchDescription
entries.doc: A launch as a source describes it. Ruimte starts what `spawn` says, in a session of its own, once a person approved it.

entries.name: defineLaunchSource
entries.doc: Needs `launches.provide`. Proposed: name `launchSources` under `proposed` in the manifest, and the id under `provides.launchSources`, which starts `server/` once a project's launches are read. Its launches show beside a person's own, under `title`, and start only after a person approved them on this machine: the command, the folder, the variables and the fingerprint together. At most 64 launches per source. Throws for an id the manifest does not list.

entries.name: MachineCandidate
entries.doc: A place a machine can run in, as a source lists it: a container, a volume, another system on this computer.

entries.name: MachineStep
entries.doc: One program Ruimte runs on this machine, to its end, on the way to a machine in that place.

entries.name: MachineStart
entries.doc: How a machine gets into a place and starts there. The extension describes it; Ruimte runs it, after a person approved it.

entries.name: PrepareContext
defineMachineSource
entries.doc: Needs `machines.provide`. Proposed: name `machineSources` under `proposed` in the manifest, and the id under `provides.machineSources`. Its places show in Settings, Machines of the app on this computer, under `title`. A start asks `start` what to run, and runs it only after a person approved the programs, their folder, their variables and the fingerprint together. The new machine has an identity of its own and signs itself onto the account of the machine that started it, through `inside`, on that same approval: no call hands an extension a key, a token, a registration or a connection to it, and nothing mounts the login of a CLI on this computer into it. A start with `inside` on a machine that is on no account ends before anything runs. Ruimte stops or removes nothing a start made. At most 16 places per source. Throws for an id the manifest does not list.

entries.name: Notification
entries.doc: What Ruimte tells a person about an agent, as a channel is handed it.

entries.name: defineNotificationChannel
entries.doc: Needs `notifications.provide`. Proposed: name `notificationChannels` under `proposed` in the manifest, and the id under `provides.notificationChannels`. A channel shows under Settings, Notifications of the app on this computer and is off until a person turns it on. Ruimte decides when: `deliver` runs when a phone would get the push, so it waits while the person is at a desktop and skips what they read or snoozed there. The channel only delivers. One that throws or does not settle in time loses that one notification, with a line in the extension's log. Throws for an id the manifest does not list.
entries.code: export function defineNotificationChannel(channel: { id: string; title: string; deliver(notification: Notification): void | Promise<void> }): void;

entries.name: defineUiSource
entries.doc: Needs `ui.provide`. Proposed: name `uiSources` under `proposed` in the manifest, and the id under `provides.uiSources`. Live data for a block an agent writes in a chat: the agent reads it as `@Query("extension", { source: "<extension id>/<id>", args: { ... } })` and the components Ruimte already has draw the answer. `description` (at most 200 characters) and `parameters`, a JSON Schema of `args` (at most 2 KB), are what the agent is told. `read` gets the arguments as the block wrote them, so check them, and the project of the chat that wrote the block. It only reads: a block is read again on its own, by every client that shows it. Its answer is JSON of at most 32 KB; a larger one, a throw and an answer that takes too long show as a failed read in the block. Throws for an id the manifest does not list.

entries.name: defineAgentProvider
entries.doc: Needs `agents.provide`. Proposed: name `agentProviders` under `proposed` in the manifest, and the id under `provides.agentProviders`. An agent that speaks the Agent Client Protocol on its standard input and output, offered in the model pickers beside the agents Ruimte knows. You describe and Ruimte starts: `spawn` answers the program once, as your server part loads, and Ruimte runs it for each chat in that chat's own folder, so `cwd` of the description is not used. `models` names what the picker offers until the agent reports its own in a chat, at most 64; without it the picker has one entry, Default. Ruimte hands the agent no key and reads none: it signs in the way it does on its own. The extension's id and this id together are at most 29 characters. Throws for an id the manifest does not list.

entries.name: ReferenceItem
entries.doc: A thing a reference lists after `#`: `id` is its own within the reference, `name` is what a person picks it by.

entries.name: defineReference
entries.doc: Needs `composer.provide`. Proposed: name `references` under `proposed` in the manifest, and the id under `provides.references`. Things from outside the project for `#` in a chat, as `defineReference` of `client/` offers them, from the machine: they also show on a phone and in a window that did not load your `client/`. Picking one puts what `read` answers in the prompt, which the person still sends. `list` answers at most 200 things, and `read` at most 100,000 characters. A reference both parts define under one id shows once. Throws for an id the manifest does not list.

entries.name: defineSlashCommand
entries.doc: Needs `composer.provide`. Proposed: name `slashCommands` under `proposed` in the manifest, and the name under `provides.slashCommands`. After `/` in a chat, as `defineSlashCommand` of `client/` offers it, from the machine. `name` is of lowercase letters, digits and dashes. It expands into the prompt, at most 100,000 characters, and the person still sends it: a command starts nothing and sends nothing. A command both parts define under one name shows once. Throws for a name the manifest does not list.

entries.name: Problem
entries.doc: A place in a file, counted from 1 as a person reads it, and what is wrong there.

entries.name: FileProblems
defineProblemSource
entries.doc: Needs `problems.provide`. Proposed: name `problemSources` under `proposed` in the manifest, and the id under `provides.problemSources`. Names a source `problems.report` speaks for; its problems show under `title`. Throws for an id the manifest does not list.
entries.code: export function defineProblemSource(source: { id: string; title: string }): void;

entries.name: problems
entries.doc: Needs `problems.provide`. The problems of a source show with the editor's own and in what an agent reads of the project. The machine keeps them in memory, until the project closes or the extension is turned off, changed or removed.

files

terminals
storage
projectSettings

entries.name: secrets
entries.doc: Kept readable only by the person who runs the machine.

entries.name: machine
defineLanguageServer
entries.doc: Needs `languages.servers`. Adds a server, listed in Settings like one a person added, and started without asking: installing the extension was the approval. Calling it again with the same name changes it, and removing the extension removes it unless a person edited it.

entries.name: TestNode
entries.doc: A node of the project a test host starts with. Only `id` is needed: a node is a note on the first view unless it says otherwise.

entries.name: TestSubagent
entries.doc: A sub-agent at work for a chat: running unless it says otherwise, and `node` the id of the node of a task's child.

entries.name: TestHostAnswers
entries.doc: What the machine and the person answer the client in a test. A call that asks the machine gets what it was asked and returns the value; throw `refusal(code, message)` to answer a failure. A call nothing answers is `unavailable`, except where the test host keeps the state itself: the canvas, views, storage, settings, and what an agent reads of a node with `text`.

entries.name: TestHostOptions
TestSlotShown
entries.doc: How a slot shows a definition at a place, after its function answered.

entries.name: TestMenuItem
entries.doc: A row of a menu as a person sees it. `run` answers as `run` of the test host does.
entries.code: export type TestMenuItem = 'separator' | { title: string; checked?: boolean; run(): Promise<Result<void>> } | { title: string; items: TestMenuItem[] };

entries.name: TestCall
entries.doc: What a test host recorded of a call of the API that answers a Result.

entries.name: TestScreen
entries.doc: Each step lets React finish inside `act` and waits on no timer, so it works under `jest.useFakeTimers()` too.

entries.name: TestDefinition
entries.doc: What the extension gave a `define*`, as it gave it.

entries.name: TestEditorDecoration
entries.doc: A mark in the margin of an editor a test opened, with the id of the decoration that put it there and its last line filled in.

entries.name: TestHost
createTestHost
entries.doc: A client of Ruimte in this process, with a project in memory you seed: it loads `client/index.ts` afresh, records what the extension defines and does, answers what you script and refuses with the permissions of your manifest, in the messages and codes Ruimte gives. What it loaded speaks for it, and a file your test imports itself speaks for the test host created last.
entries.code: export function createTestHost(options?: TestHostOptions): Promise<TestHost>;

entries.name: TestServerAnswers
entries.doc: What the machine answers `server/` in a test. Each answer gets what `server/` asked and returns the value; throw `refusal(code, message)` to answer a failure. A call nothing answers is `unavailable`.

entries.name: Method
TestServer
createTestServer
entries.doc: Loads `server/index.ts` in this process, against the machine of a test: storage in memory, answers you script and the permissions of your manifest, refused with the messages and codes Ruimte gives. Each test server loads `server/index.ts` afresh, with every file of your project it imports, so no state carries over; a package from `node_modules` loads once. What it loaded speaks for it, and a file your test imports itself speaks for the test server created last.
entries.code: export function createTestServer<Api = Record<string, (...args: never[]) => Promise<unknown>>>(options?: TestServerOptions): Promise<TestServer<Api>>;
